# Jonah Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 340r–340v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JON_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** And-was the-word of-YHWH to Yonah [Jonah] son of-Amittai, saying: **1:2** "Arise [qum], go [lekh] to Nineveh [Nineveh], the-city the-great [ha-ir ha-gedolah], and-call [qera] against-her, for their-evil [ra'atam] has-come-up [altah] before-me [lefanai]."

**1:3** And-rose Yonah to-flee [livroach] to-Tarshish [Tarshish] from-the-presence [mi-lifnei] of-YHWH; and-went-down [vayyered] to-Yafo [Joppa], and-found a-ship [oniyyah] going [ba'ah] to-Tarshish, and-gave her-fare [sekhara], and-went-down [vayyered] into-her to-go with-them to-Tarshish from-the-presence of-YHWH.

**1:4** And-YHWH hurled [hetil] a-great wind [ruach gedolah] to the-sea, and-there-was a-great storm [sa'ar gadol] on-the-sea, and-the-ship thought [chishvah] to-be-broken [lehishaver].

**1:5** And-the-sailors [ha-mallachim] were-afraid [vayire'u] and-cried-out [vayiz'aqu] each [ish] to his-god [elohav], and-they-hurled [vayatilu] the-vessels [kelim] which [were] in-the-ship to the-sea to-lighten [lehaqel] from-upon-them. And-Yonah went-down [yarad] to the-innermost-parts [yarketei] of-the-vessel [ha-sefinah], and-lay-down [vayishkav] and-fell-fast-asleep [vayeradam].

**1:6** And-drew-near [vayiqrav] to-him the-chief of-the-sailors [rav ha-chovel] and-said to-him, "What [is] to-you, O-sleeper [nirdam]? Arise [qum], call [qera] to your-god [elohekha]; perhaps the-god [ha-elohim] will-give-thought [yitashet] to-us and-we-will-not perish [noved]."

**1:7** And-they-said each [ish] to his-companion [re'ehu], "Come [lekhu] and-let-us-cast lots [goral], and-we-will-know [veneda] on-account-of-whom [beshel-mi] this-evil [ha-ra'ah] [is] upon-us." And-they-cast lots [vayyapilu goralot], and-the-lot fell [vayyippol ha-goral] on Yonah.

**1:8** And-they-said to-him, "Tell [haggida] us, please, on-account-of-whom [ba-asher le-mi] this-evil [ha-ra'ah] [is] upon-us? What [is] your-occupation [melakhtekha]? And-from-where [me-ayin] do-you-come? What [is] your-land [artsekha]? And-from-what people [am] [are] you?"

**1:9** And-he-said to-them, "A-Hebrew [ivri] I [am], and-YHWH the-God of-the-heavens [elohei ha-shamayim] I fear [yarei] — who made [asah] the-sea [ha-yam] and-the-dry-land [ha-yabbashah]."

**1:10** And-the-men feared [vayire'u] a-great fear [yirah gedolah] and-said to-him, "What [is] this you-have-done [asita]?" For the-men knew [yade'u] that from-the-presence of-YHWH he [was] fleeing [bore'ach], for he-had-told [higgid] them.

**1:11** And-they-said to-him, "What shall-we-do [na'aseh] to-you, that the-sea may-be-still [veyishtok] from-upon-us?" For the-sea [was] going [holekh] and-storming [so'er].

**1:12** And-he-said to-them, "Lift-me-up [sa'uni] and-hurl-me [vehatilyuni] to the-sea, and-the-sea will-be-still [veyishtok] from-upon-you; for I know [yode'a] that on-account-of-me [beshelli] this-great storm [ha-sa'ar ha-gadol] [is] upon-you."

**1:13** And-the-men rowed [vayachteru] to-return [lehashiv] to the-dry-land [ha-yabbashah], and-they-could not [lo yakholu], for the-sea [was] going and-storming upon-them.

**1:14** And-they-called [vayiqre'u] to YHWH and-said, "Please [ana], YHWH, let-us-not perish [al-na novdah] on-account-of the-life [nefesh] of-this man, and-do-not put [al-titten] upon-us innocent [naqi] blood [dam]; for you, YHWH, as you-have-pleased [chafatsta] you-have-done [asita]."

**1:15** And-they-lifted [vayyis'u] Yonah and-hurled-him [vayatiluhu] to the-sea, and-the-sea stood-still [vayyaamod] from-its-raging [mi-za'po].

**1:16** And-the-men feared [vayire'u] a-great fear [yirah gedolah] [of] YHWH, and-they-sacrificed [vayyizbechu] a-sacrifice [zevach] to-YHWH, and-vowed [vayyidru] vows [nedarim].

**1:17** And-YHWH appointed [vayman] a-great fish [dag gadol] to-swallow [livlo'a] Yonah; and-Yonah was in-the-belly [bim'ei] of-the-fish three days and-three nights.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "went down":** The verb *yarad* ("went down") appears three times in this verse — Jonah goes *down* to Joppa, *down* into the ship. The descent motif continues in v.5 (*down* into the hold) and ch.2 (*down* to the depths). Jonah's flight from YHWH is a continuous downward spiral.

**v.4 — "the ship thought":** The Hebrew *ha-oniyyah chishvah* literally says the ship "thought" or "reckoned" it would break apart. This is a striking personification — the ship itself senses the danger.

**v.9 — "a Hebrew I am":** *Ivri* — the term used for Israelites by foreigners or when speaking to foreigners. Jonah's theological confession is ironic: he confesses belief in the God of sea and land while fleeing across the sea from that God.

**v.17 — "appointed":** The verb *vayman* (from *manah*, "to appoint/assign") — the same verb will recur for the plant (4:6), the worm (4:7), and the east wind (4:8). God "appoints" elements of creation to teach Jonah.

*— EMET*
